notes.yagenda: O- for he or she in the past.

guidebook.intro: Talk about what you did. **Dong** marks something already done, and **onongo** sets a scene in the past.

tips.title: Acamo dong: I have eaten
body: **Dong** after the verb means already: **Acamo dong** (I have eaten), **Atyeko** (I have finished). The plain verb with a time word is the past: **Lawoo acito i taun** (yesterday I went to town).

tips.title: Onongo: it was
body: **Onongo** puts a state in the past: **Con onongo abedo lakwan** (long ago I was a student), **Lawoo onongo atye gang** (yesterday I was at home).
He and she take **o-** in the past: **ocito** (he went), and they take **gi-**: **gioo** (they arrived).

culture.title: Icamo dong?
body: **Icamo dong?** (have you eaten?) is a caring question, not small talk. If you say no, expect to be fed.
